plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in eastern Australia turn lavender-blue when this tree flowers. Its bare or nearly bare branches carry clouds of trumpet-shaped blossoms. Petals drift down to cover the pavement in a violet carpet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late October through November, which is late spring in the Southern Hemisphere. Peak bloom is usually in early November, and many trees are still flowering or shedding petals around November 22.
plants.location: Eastern Australia, including Brisbane and Sydney, where it is widely planted as a street tree. It is native to South America.
plants.funFact: Jacarandas often flower before the leaves fully emerge. That is why the color looks so solid from a distance, and why the tree's bloom has become a seasonal landmark in many Australian cities.
